description: We’re a team of innovators aiming to make space exploration intresting and fun.
summary:
Solar Flare: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive 3D web platform created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Over six decades of space exploration have left iconic landers, rovers, and stations resting quietly across our solar system. While these pioneers often fade from public awareness, Solar Flare brings their legacies back to life.

Powered by Three.js and WebGL, the platform lets users seamlessly explore three planetary bodies: Earth, the Moon, and Mars. Visitors can freely orbit each world, discover 18 mapped historic missions, and interact with glowing coordinate pins. Selecting a pin opens an archival dossier featuring authentic NASA imagery, launch telemetry, and curated mission highlights.

A central innovation is its dual-tier accessibility. Synchronized audio narration reads stories hands-free, with ambient music ducking beneath the voice. Meanwhile, an intelligent age-aware engine dynamically calibrates storytelling depth between a youth mode and a scientific mode, so every visitor gets the right level of detail.

Privacy-first, responsive, and requiring zero installation, Solar Flare ensures humanity’s boldest robotic emissaries are forever celebrated rather than forgotten.
details:
Solar Flare: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive 3D web platform that brings humanity’s silent robotic explorers back into public memory. Over six decades of space exploration have left landers, rovers, and stations resting across Earth, the Moon, and Mars, and most people have never heard their stories. Solar Flare lets anyone explore three planetary bodies, freely orbit each world, and discover 18 mapped historic missions through glowing coordinate pins. Selecting a pin opens an archival dossier with authentic NASA imagery, launch telemetry, and curated mission highlights, turning scattered historical data into one immersive experience.

The platform’s central innovation is its dual-tier accessibility. Synchronized audio narration reads each mission story hands-free, while ambient music automatically ducks beneath the voice so the narration stays clear. Alongside this, an intelligent age-aware engine dynamically calibrates storytelling depth between a youth mode, which uses simple language and a sense of wonder, and a scientific mode, which offers technical detail and precise mission data. This means a curious child, a student, and a space enthusiast can each get a fitting experience from the same platform.

The benefits are practical as well as educational. Solar Flare requires zero installation and runs in any modern browser, so it works on classroom computers, personal laptops, and phones without barriers. It is responsive across screen sizes and privacy-first, collecting no unnecessary personal data. By supporting both audio and visual learning, it also serves users with different accessibility needs.

We built the platform with Three.js and WebGL for real-time 3D rendering, using planetary textures and accurate coordinates to place each mission pin where it truly landed. The interface, narration system, and age-aware storytelling logic were developed with standard web technologies, keeping the project lightweight and easy to share. Throughout development, our team weighed performance, accuracy of historical data, accessibility, and ease of use, making sure the experience stays smooth even on modest devices.

The project is creative because it reframes abandoned hardware as characters with stories rather than forgotten debris. Glowing pins turn the surface of each world into a map of human ambition, and adaptive storytelling makes the content personal to each visitor. Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space history, strengthen science education, and ensure that humanity’s boldest robotic emissaries are celebrated rather than forgotten.
